title: The recording session: the A&R man with perfect ears
summary: Four tunes made a date; a brilliant A&R man stopped squeaks and suggested slowing the minor tune.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So we made... In those early days, you had to record four songs to complete a date. It ain't like it is today where you go into overtime and all that stuff. Four songs... You had to make four songs to make a date. So we made the three songs first, and we saved "Minnie The Moocher" for the last. I wish I had... A book I always like to have with me is that guy's (?) that was the A&R man.
But anyway, we started out playing... We fooled around...
It wasn't Dick Jacobs, was it.
No. He seemed to be a fabulous songwriter. He was young, and he...

No, not Fred Coots. We're talking about some of the guys who... Oh, I used to take his name with me all the time. I generally take a book and look in it. But anyway, he could tell... I never recorded with nobody that had such an ear like him. He could tell which saxophone player squeaked. If he knew your reeds weren't quite wet and you squeaked, he could hear the first saxophone squeak, and he'd stop you in the middle of a recording. Because he wouldn't let... You had to go through it all the way in and start over again.

So we started playing this arrangement this guy made, and it just wasn't makin' no sense. So Cab... After about three or four times playing this other arrangement, Cab said, "Foots, did you do something on 'Minnie The Moocher'?" I said, "Yes." So I went to my little saxophone case and got out my little strips of paper, and passed them around. We didn't have but ten pieces in it, the same band he... So we started playing that. And we was playing [SINGS REFRAIN]... So the guy said...after a couple of times going
over it, he said, "I think a minor sounds better slow." So when we slowed it down... [SINGS FINAL VERSION OF REFRAIN] Right away we knew we had it. In about two or three takes we had that thing made.
